name: Delhi Sultanate, c. 1330
source: Hand-drawn approximation after Schwartzberg, A Historical Atlas of South Asia (1992), plate V.2 (p. 38), 'South Asia in the time of the Khaljis and Tughluqs, c. 1290-1390'. Shows the Sultanate under Muhammad bin Tughluq at its greatest reach, with Ma'bar (lost 1335) and Bengal (independent from 1338) included. Excludes Kashmir, Orissa (the Eastern Gangas), the Gond forests, the Hoysala plateau, Kerala and Assam. The Rajasthan desert and the Sindh frontier are drawn generously. Good first issue: trace properly from the DSAL scan.
